rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4; the authors build and run their own hybrid ConvLSTM + ECMWF S2S forecasting models for SSM (0-5 cm) and RZSM (0-100 cm) at 1-46 day leads over the Yangtze River Basin and central Europe, train on 2015-2018 and evaluate on 2019-2022 against ERA5, SMAP L4 and ISMN in situ stations (Figures 4-15).
rows.notes: The study reports only soil moisture forecasting skill (PCC, ubRMSE, bias, RMSE) of a hybrid deep learning/S2S model; it never links forecasts to crop yield forecasting, irrigation scheduling or any crop production outcome. Crop yield forecasting is mentioned only as a potential application in the Introduction/Conclusions. Moreover the forecasting inputs are ERA5 reanalysis and S2S model output, not satellite SSM retrievals (SMAP L4 is used only as an alternative reference in Figure 7), so the technology tested is not remote-sensing SSM retrieval translated to the root zone. The result is at most a precondition (soil moisture forecasts) for the claimed delivery of crop yield forecasting.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4; own model experiments forecasting SSM and RZSM 1-46 days ahead over the YRB and EU with a hybrid ConvLSTM + ECMWF S2S model, compared with SVR, RF, ConvLSTM and S2S baselines and validated against ERA5, SMAP L4 and ISMN stations (Figures 4-15).
rows.notes: The study reports skill of sub-seasonal soil moisture forecasts; it does not report any result on climate-resilient agricultural management, drought risk reduction, or any management decision or outcome. Benefits for drought early warning and agricultural adaptation are asserted in the Introduction, Section 2.1 and Conclusions, not demonstrated. The forecasting system is driven by ERA5 reanalysis and S2S model output rather than satellite SSM retrievals, so it is also not a test of translating remote-sensing SSM into root-zone information. Soil moisture forecasting is an upstream precondition of the claimed risk-management benefit.

notes: Full text available (some pages duplicated from the peer-review layout but legible). The study is a methodological soil moisture forecasting paper; neither claim's effect (crop yield forecasting / climate-resilient agricultural management) is evaluated, and the technology is hybrid DL+S2S forecasting on reanalysis data rather than remote-sensing SSM retrieval.
